facts.statement: Morsoravis was an extinct neoavian bird that lived in the Early Eocene of Denmark.
facts.quote: Morsoravis is an extinct genus of neoavian bird from the Early Eocene Fur Formation of Denmark.

facts.statement: Fossils of Morsoravis have also been found in the Green River Formation of Wyoming and possibly the Nanjemoy Formation of Virginia.
facts.quote: Fossils of Morsoravis have also been found in the Green River Formation of Wyoming and possibly the Nanjemoy Formation of Virginia.

facts.statement: Several fish bones are preserved within the body of the Morsoravis holotype, alongside other surrounding fish fossils.
facts.quote: There are several fish bones preserved within the body of the bird, although there are also other fish fossils surrounding the specimen.

facts.statement: The Morsoravis holotype was collected from the northwestern corner of the island of Mors at the base of a cliff.
facts.quote: The fossil was collected from a site on the northwestern corner of the island of Mors, at the base of a cliff.

facts.statement: The generic name Morsoravis is derived from the island name Mors, the Latin word for shore, and the Latin word for bird.
facts.quote: The generic name Morsoravis comes from Mors, the name of the island on which the holotype was collected, Latin sor, meaning "shore", and avis, meaning bird.

facts.statement: The specific epithet sedilis refers to the bird's capability to perch, derived from Latin words meaning to sit still.
facts.quote: The specific ephitet, sedilis, is from Latin "sedere", meaining to sit still, and ilis, expressing capability, referencing Morsoravis' capability to perch.

facts.statement: Morsoravis had a rounded head measuring about 31.8 mm in total length, with the relatively long beak accounting for about half of that size.
facts.quote: Morsoravis had a rounded head totalling about 31.8 mm, of which about half is accounted for by the relatively long beak, with a rounded braincase.

facts.statement: The Morsoravis beak is straight, pointed at the tip, and features an elongated nostril.
facts.quote: The beak is straight and pointed at its tip, and has an elongated nostril.

facts.statement: The schizorhinal beak of Morsoravis suggests the possibility of rhynchokinetism in the rostrum.
facts.quote: The beak is schizorhinal, suggesting the possibility of rhynchokinetism of the rostrum.

facts.statement: The orbit of Morsoravis is about the size of the braincase, and its scleral ring consists of 12 segments.
facts.quote: The orbit is about the size of the braincase, and the scleral ring is made of 12 segments.

facts.statement: Morsoravis possesses 21 presacral vertebrae that exhibit a pleurocoelous condition.
facts.quote: There are 21 presacral vertebrae, that is, vertebrae cranial of the synsacrum, which exhibit a pleurocoelous condition.

facts.statement: The tarsometatarsus of Morsoravis is similar to that of Pumiliornis and features an accessory trochlea indicative of at least semi-zygodactyly.
facts.quote: The tarsometatarsus is highly similar to that of Pumiliornis, a psittacopedid bird, and features an accessary trochlea of the trochlea of the fourth metatarsal, indicative of at least semi-zygodactyly.

facts.statement: Morsoravis has a relatively long hallux with a large, curved claw, and its toe proportions are not characteristic of ground-dwelling birds.
facts.quote: The hallux is relatively long and has a large, curved claw, and the proportions of the toes are not characteristic of ground-dwelling birds.

facts.statement: The semi-zygodactyl foot of Morsoravis has a second toe with limited side-to-side motion, likely an adaptation for climbing.
facts.quote: The semi-zygodactyl foot also has a second toe with relatively little freedom of side-to-side motion, likely an adaptation for climbing.

facts.statement: Mayr (2023) established the new family Morsoravidae with Morsoravis as the type genus, including Pumiliornis and Sororavis.
facts.quote: Mayr (2023) described a new family, Morsoravidae, with Morsoravis as the type genus, and including Pumiliornis and Sororavis, to the exclusion of the other birds previously described as psittacopedids.

facts.statement: Morsoravis lived during the Ypresian stage, from 56 to 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The holotype of Morsoravis, MGUH 28930, consists of a complete but fully articulated and three-dimensionally preserved skeleton, found in the marine Fur Formation of Denmark.
